title: Shipment Reconciliation
statement: A warehouse scans every item it ships, and the store scans every item it receives. Both scans are lists of SKU codes, and the same SKU can appear many times.

Report every SKU whose counts don't match as `"SKU:+d"` or `"SKU:-d"`, where `d` is how many more (`+`) or fewer (`-`) items the store received than the warehouse shipped. Return the reports sorted by SKU in plain character order.

examples.explanation: Every count matches, so there's nothing to report.

constraints: SKUs are 1 to 12 characters of uppercase letters, digits, and hyphens

hints: Comparing every shipped item with every received item is quadratic. What could you count instead?
Use one hash map from SKU to a net count: plus one for each received item, minus one for each shipped item.
Keep only the SKUs whose net count isn't zero, sort them, and write the sign explicitly, including the plus.
pitfalls: Missing SKUs that appear in only one of the lists.
Dropping the + sign on positive differences.
Sorting SKUs that look numeric as numbers, so K-10 and K-2 come out in the wrong order.
Reporting SKUs whose difference is zero.
interviewerNotes: Ask whether one map is enough or they need two.
Ask what the sort costs and why it's over distinct SKUs, not all items.
Follow-up: the scans are too big for memory. Strong answers mention sorting both files and merging, or partitioning by hash.
